content.user_title: Harden CTF Challenges Against LLM Shortcuts
content.value_statement: Challenge authors need to reduce shallow LLM pattern matching without making fair challenges frustrating. This skill reproduces the intended solve, selects a small resistance change, and verifies the result end to end.
actual_capabilities: Reproduce an authorized challenge baseline through its player-facing interface.
Identify one cheap LLM shortcut using evidence from the baseline solve.
Select a lightweight pattern break, runtime discovery, context split, state dependency, or semantic decoy.
Apply human-cost gates that preserve the vulnerability class and learning objective.
Verify application behavior, transformed solves, flags, and shortcut reduction end to end.
Produce a concise report with status, difficulty, verification, and changed files.
limitations: It is intended only for authorized CTFs, training labs, and test systems.
It does not replace expert review of challenge isolation, deployment, or infrastructure security.
It cannot prove that a challenge resists every model or independent solver.
It requires enough challenge documentation and access to reproduce the baseline.

use_cases.title: Review a Training Challenge
use_cases.description: Reproduce a lab solve, identify the fastest shallow shortcut, and propose a small change that preserves the lesson.

use_cases.title: Validate a Challenge Update
use_cases.description: Check that a transformed challenge still starts, exposes the intended weakness, and produces the expected result.

use_cases.title: Improve LLM-Assisted Practice
use_cases.description: Reduce obvious model shortcuts while keeping the expected human knowledge, actions, and difficulty band stable.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Review the Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authorized CTF challenge. Record its vulnerability class, intended solve path, required knowledge, difficulty band, and clean-start procedure. Do not modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Find the Shortcut
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the verified baseline evidence, identify the single cheapest LLM shortcut. Explain which player-facing clue enables it and why the shortcut does not represent the intended learning objective.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after reproducing the original solve.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Design a Small Resistance
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the smallest resistance move that reduces the identified shortcut. Check the same vulnerability class, learning objective, prerequisite knowledge, and human-cost gate before proposing the change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the baseline shortcut is clearly evidenced.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Verify the Transformation
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the transformed challenge from a clean state. Check startup, legitimate behavior, intended vulnerability, shortcut reduction, runtime success, flag isolation, and independent-solver status. Produce the required final report.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after implementing a challenge change.

output_examples.input: An authorized web challenge exposes an object identifier in a static response, making the intended authorization weakness immediately obvious.
output_examples.output: Shortcut identified: static object disclosure. Recommended move: reveal the identifier through ordinary runtime activity, adding one observation without changing the vulnerability.

output_examples.input: A proposed transformation adds a five-step state machine and requires an unrelated protocol.
output_examples.output: Rejected by the Human Cost Gate. It adds a new exploit primitive and materially increases player effort, so the original challenge should remain unchanged.

output_examples.input: The transformed challenge starts normally, preserves the weakness, removes the static cue, and passes an end-to-end solve.
output_examples.output: TRANSFORMED PASS. The report records the baseline, selected resistance, human-cost estimate, post-change difficulty, verification result, and changed files.

best_practices: Start with a clean, reproducible baseline before proposing any change.
Prefer one evidence-based resistance move with one to three additional meaningful actions.
Verify the intended solve, flag isolation, and normal application behavior after every change.
anti_patterns: Do not hide flags behind randomness, unstable behavior, or undiscoverable values.
Do not stack decoys, brute force, CAPTCHA, token flooding, or unrelated trivia.
Do not claim LLM resistance without an isolated fresh-solver check or an explicit NOT TESTED result.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: CTF authors, security trainers, and curriculum designers who maintain authorized challenges can use it.

faq.question: Does it create new vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It preserves the original vulnerability class and learning objective while reducing one shallow shortcut.

faq.question: Can it test production systems?
faq.answer: Only with explicit authorization. The workflow is designed for CTFs, training labs, and authorized test systems.

faq.question: How many changes should it make?
faq.answer: It defaults to zero or one lightweight change. A second change requires evidence and must pass the human-cost gate.

faq.question: How does it verify success?
faq.answer: It restarts from a clean state and checks startup, normal behavior, the intended weakness, shortcut reduction, runtime success, and flag isolation.

faq.question: Does self-review prove model resistance?
faq.answer: No. A genuinely isolated fresh solver is preferred. Without one, the report must state NOT TESTED.
